STS31_BASE_CERTIFICATE.canonical_base_definition: Points are the 31 nonzero vectors of F_2^5. A block/line is an unordered triple {u,v,u+v} for distinct nonzero u,v. B is the point-block Levi incidence graph.

proofs.replication: For a fixed point, the other 30 points are partitioned into pairs by the unique blocks through that point, so r=(31-1)/(3-1)=15.
proofs.simple_bipartite: Levi vertices are distinct point identities and block identities; an incidence is a set-membership relation, giving a simple bipartite graph.
proofs.C4_free: A simple 4-cycle would put two distinct points in two distinct blocks, contradicting lambda=1 uniqueness of the block containing a point pair.
proofs.connected: Any two point vertices share their unique block and are at distance 2; every block is adjacent to three points.
proofs.incidence_matrix: For the 31x155 incidence matrix N, diagonal row inner products are 15 and off-diagonal row inner products are 1; hence NN^T=14I+J.
proofs.singular_spectrum: NN^T has eigenvalue 45 on the all-ones vector and eigenvalue 14 with multiplicity 30, so N has nonzero singular values sqrt(45) once and sqrt(14) with multiplicity 30.
proofs.Levi_spectrum: Adjacency spectrum is +/-sqrt(45), +/-sqrt(14) (multiplicity 30 each), and zero with the remaining multiplicity.
proofs.Ramanujan_threshold: The (15,3)-biregular universal tree has spectral radius rho=sqrt(15-1)+sqrt(3-1)=sqrt(14)+sqrt(2). Since sqrt(14)<rho, all nontrivial base eigenvalues lie in the bipartite Ramanujan interval.

external_theorem_binding.source: Chris Hall, Doron Puder, William F. Sawin, Ramanujan Coverings of Graphs, Advances in Mathematics 323 (2018), 367-410, DOI 10.1016/j.aim.2017.10.042, arXiv:1506.02335v4
external_theorem_binding.exact_imported_claim: Every connected loopless graph has a one-sided Ramanujan r-covering for every r>=1; every covering of a bipartite graph is bipartite, so every connected bipartite graph has a fully Ramanujan r-covering for every r.

derived_cover_lemmas.degrees_preserved: A graph covering is a local bijection on incident edges, hence every point-sheet vertex has degree 15 and every block-sheet vertex degree 3.
derived_cover_lemmas.bipartite_preserved: Pull back the point/block bipartition through the covering map.
derived_cover_lemmas.simple_preserved: A loop upstairs would project to a loop downstairs. Two parallel lifted edges incident to the same lifted vertex would map to the same base incidence, violating local injectivity because the base is simple.
derived_cover_lemmas.C4_free_preserved: A lifted simple 4-cycle projects to a closed non-backtracking walk of length 4: immediate projected backtracking is forbidden by local injectivity. In a simple bipartite C4-free base such a reduced closed length-4 walk cannot exist.
derived_cover_lemmas.Ramanujan_preserved: HPS bounds all new eigenvalues; bipartiteness makes new spectrum symmetric. Old nontrivial eigenvalues are those of the already-Ramanujan base, so the lift is bipartite Ramanujan.
derived_cover_lemmas.connectedness: If an r-cover had c>1 connected components, each component covering the connected (15,3)-biregular base contributes Perron eigenvalue sqrt(45). Only one copy belongs to the old lifted base eigenspace; an additional +sqrt(45) is therefore new. Since sqrt(45)>sqrt(14)+sqrt(2), this contradicts the HPS Ramanujan new-spectrum bound. Thus every HPS-good cover of this base is connected.

RAMANUJAN_TO_TREEWIDTH_CHAIN.spectral_gap: For a connected (15,3)-biregular Ramanujan cover, every nontrivial normalized-adjacency eigenvalue has absolute value at most theta<1, hence normalized Laplacian lambda_2>=gamma>0.
RAMANUJAN_TO_TREEWIDTH_CHAIN.conductance_derivation: For every S with vol(S)<=W/2, the two-level Rayleigh test gives lambda_2 <= |E(S,V\S)|*W/(vol(S)vol(V\S)); since vol(V\S)>=W/2, conductance Phi>=lambda_2/2>=gamma/2=Phi0.
RAMANUJAN_TO_TREEWIDTH_CHAIN.weighted_separator_derivation: A width-k tree decomposition has a bag X of size at most k+1 that is 1/2-balanced for the vertex weights deg(v). For every component C of G-X, vol(C)<=W/2, so |E(C,X)|>=Phi0 vol(C). Summing components yields |E(V\X,X)|>=Phi0(W-vol(X)), while |E(V\X,X)|<=vol(X)<=Delta|X|. Therefore |X|>=Phi0 W/[Delta(1+Phi0)].
RAMANUJAN_TO_TREEWIDTH_CHAIN.firewall: This is a graph theorem conditional on selecting an HPS-good cover; it is not yet an explicit deterministic family theorem and does not promote H3.

findings: HPS proves existence of a Ramanujan r-cover for every r by interlacing/averaging over r-covers; it does not state the required deterministic output-polynomial selector for an arbitrary fixed base.

HPS models all r-covers by S_r edge labels; for the fixed STS31 Levi base with 465 edges this raw space has (r!)^465 labelings, so fixed base size does not make exhaustive search polynomial in the O(r)-vertex output size.

HPS v4 Remark 1.13 discusses smaller permutation groups as a possible route to relatively fast construction, but the sufficient group-representation hypotheses are not established there for the proposed PSL_2 example.
Iterated existence of good 2-lifts gives an existential powers-of-two tower route, but no source-bound polynomial-time selector for the good 2-lift at each growing stage was found in this audit.
Targeted searches through 2026 found no later theorem that directly closes deterministic output-polynomial HPS-good r-cover selection for this arbitrary fixed base.

GM_SHORTCUT_AUDIT.source: Aurelien Gribinski and Adam W. Marcus, Existence and polynomial time construction of biregular, bipartite Ramanujan graphs of all degrees, arXiv:2108.02534 (2021)
GM_SHORTCUT_AUDIT.verified_strength: For fixed k=5,d=3 their framework yields degree pair (15,3) and a deterministic polynomial-time construction in the size parameter.
GM_SHORTCUT_AUDIT.killer_gap: The source construction is a union of d k-claw matchings and explicitly includes leaf graphs formed with repetitions; no source-bound simplicity, girth>4, or C4-free guarantee was found.
GM_SHORTCUT_AUDIT.rule: If a later theorem/refinement provides simple+C4-free exact-(15,3) GM outputs with deterministic polynomial construction, the HPS-selector route must lose before construction.

BA16_IDENTITY_COLLAPSE_AUDIT.cover_projection: (base_vertex,sheet_id) -> base_vertex collapses many lifted identities to one base identity.
BA16_IDENTITY_COLLAPSE_AUDIT.reason: A quotient/projection map is not a tree decomposition, separator, minor-width upper-bound certificate, or any other legal low-treewidth proof.
BA16_IDENTITY_COLLAPSE_AUDIT.provenance_note: The exact historical BA16 repo artifact containing this phrase was not resolved by repository text/commit search in this pass; the rule is preserved here because it was explicitly supplied for this audit, with no invented source binding.

CAPTAIN_OBVIOUS_MINIMAL_DEBT.plain_answer: After the base, cover-preservation, reducer-stability and width consequences are closed, what remains is an efficient deterministic way to choose the good Ramanujan cover.

next_action_if_sealed: Proceed only to the already-authorized replacement-family preregistration, freezing the selector as the dominant unproved obligation; do not attempt construction in that preregistration.
